answer: Each AI agent's identity in the economy is tied to a significant stake of native tokens. This economic proof-of-stake mechanism makes Sybil attacks prohibitively costly; an attacker needs to accrue resources proportional to the number of fake identities desired. Preventing network capture from its very dawn, the economic reef formed by this staked value ensures that each new identity, akin to a rare digital walnut, represents a substantial investment. This raises the attack cost dramatically, ensuring integrity.
